    1. RewardWeights()

Class RewardWeights

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.curriculum.RewardWeights
public final class RewardWeights extends Object
Weights of every reward term. Each stage turns on the terms for the skill it teaches. All of these are computed from ground truth that the acting network never sees.

    • answer

      public float answer
      For answering a hit with a swing: paid once per hit taken, for the first swing made within answerWindowTicks ticks of it with the opponent no farther off than answerWithin, whether that swing lands or cuts the air. A fighter that only swings when it is sure of the hit stops swinging exactly when it is being comboed, which is when a swing is worth trying.

      That distance is a sword's reach and a little more: a swing at an opponent that is plainly out of reach answers nothing. What to do then is to get clear and come back, see comboEscape.

      It cannot be collected on: there is one per hit taken, and a hit taken costs several times as much. For the same stretch of ticks nothing else about swinging is charged either: not swinging before the weapon is back, not swinging before the plan said, not a slow hit. And the aim counts the whole time, also while the weapon recharges, since it has to find the opponent again.

    • comboEscape

      public float comboEscape
      The other way out of a combo: backing out of it and coming back with a hit. From the moment it has taken comboEscapeAfter hits in a row, which is when the opponent has a combo going. Earned when that combo then ends because the opponent could not land another hit, which is what happens when the fighter lets itself be knocked clear (W let go, backing off or stepping aside) instead of running back into the next hit. Hitting back is paid as well (comboBreak), so it is free to do whichever the moment allows: swing if the opponent is in reach, step out if it is not.

      So that backing off cannot be collected on, it is hedged twice. The bonus is only paid once the fighter has come back and landed a fully charged hit; being hit first forfeits it. And after one such escape nothing about backing off is paid again until it has landed a fully charged hit.

      It need not wait for the opponent's combo to run out. Having been clear of it for a few ticks and then landing a fully charged hit before the opponent lands another is the same thing done faster, and is paid the same (in place of comboBreak, not on top of it).

    • comboBack

      public float comboBack
      How backing out is done: with S. Per tick of holding S while backing out, for the first comboBackTicks ticks after each hit of the combo, with the opponent no farther off than comboBackWithin. Those are the ticks that decide it: the hit has thrown the fighter back, the opponent is running after it, and whether its next swing finds the fighter a step out of reach or a step inside it depends on the key held on the way. W held there carries it straight back into the next hit. For the same ticks coming back in is not paid (reengage).

      What a hit's worth of this comes to stays below what the hit cost (hitTaken), so standing with its back to the wall and being hit is never a way to collect.

    • wastedJump

      public float wastedJump
      Charged once for a jump that was not a sure thing and came to nothing: it took off with the opponent farther away than in its face (RewardModel.IN_FACE), and was back on the ground without a critical hit. From there a sprint hit is on, and a jump gives that up along with the footwork for half a second: so it has to come off, and with a critical hit paying crit it is worth making where it comes off better than about one time in three. That is the line between the two ways of hitting, and where it runs is found in the fights.

      A jump that took off with the opponent in its face is not charged, whatever came of it: mistimed, or the opponent got away while it was in the air. That costs the hit it could have been and nothing more, so that a fighter is not taught out of jumping by opponents that move. (0.13.1 and 0.13.2 charged by whether the opponent was in reach on the way down, wherever the jump was made from. In fights that was nearly every jump, and the jump was gone within fifteen updates of leaving the drills.)

      Only a cost, so there is nothing in it to collect on. What keeps the jump alive is what a critical hit pays (crit).

      It has to be of the same order as that. In 0.13.0 it was a seventh of what a critical hit earns, and two things followed. A jump was worth making wherever a critical hit came of it one time in eight, which is a jump at an opponent four blocks off. And what is learned from a batch of fights goes by how far each outcome is from the average: next to the critical hits, a cost that small all but vanished, while every critical hit landed from close up made jumping likelier everywhere. So it kept jumping at an opponent out of reach long after it had the timing.

    • jumpFreeWithin

      public float jumpFreeWithin
      A jump taken off with the opponent no farther away than this is never charged as wasted, whatever came of it (RewardModel.IN_FACE up to 0.13.3, when a jump was only wanted from right in the opponent's face). Zero: every jump that ends without a critical hit is charged wastedJump, which is then set low; where a jump is worth making is left to what critical hits pay.

    • airWhiff

      public float airWhiff
      Charged for a swing made in the air that reaches nothing: the opponent was not under the crosshair, or too far off. Only in the air. A swing on the ground that misses still costs nothing but the weapon's charge, as before.

      In the air it is different in two ways. The swing there is the one a critical hit is made of, and it comes at the end of a jump or a knock-up that has taken half a second; and the weapon it uses up is the one the fighter needs the moment it lands, when an opponent that was out of reach arrives. Without a cost nothing ever told the crit model that such a swing is a bad one: held in place for a drill it loses nothing by it, and after being knocked up by a hit there is not even a jump to be charged for.

    • airWhiffBeyond

      public float airWhiffBeyond
      Above zero: a swing in the air that reaches nothing is only charged airWhiff if the opponent was farther away than this when it was made. Nearer than that it was an attempt: the opponent was at the edge of the sword's reach or a step beyond it, which is where an opponent that is comboing the fighter stands, and where a person is a tick late or half a step too close every few swings. Such a swing costs the sword's charge and nothing else, so that whether it is worth making is learned from how often it lands. Zero: every swing in the air at nothing is charged.

      Up to the first runs of 0.14.0 every one was charged, at 1.0. Comboed by a person, who keeps at three blocks, it was in the air from one hit to the next and did not swing once.

    • comboAsCrit

      public float comboAsCrit
      The other way to the same damage. Paid each time the hits of one combo that were not critical add up to another critical hit's worth of damage, for as long as the combo lasts. So a sprint hit that is followed up earns what a critical hit earns, hit for hit and damage for damage, and a sprint hit that stays alone earns less: it did less than a critical hit would have.

      This is what makes not jumping a choice with something behind it. Where a critical hit is not a sure thing the jump is left alone, the sprint-hit fighter plays on, and if its combo comes to as much as the critical hit would have, that was the right call and is paid as one.

      It is counted in damage done, and paid again for every further critical hit's worth, so a long combo is worth more than several short ones and there is nothing to gain by breaking one off to start the count again. A hit made before the weapon was back counts for nothing here, as it does for the combo.

    • critReady

      public float critReady
      Per tick of being set up for a critical hit as the weapon comes back: falling, not sprinting as far as the server knows, the weapon nearly recharged and the opponent within critReadyWithin. It is to a critical hit what primed is to a sprint hit, and is paid out of the same few ticks per landed hit, so a fighter is paid for the one or the other and hopping about without ever hitting earns nothing.

      For the jump a critical hit starts with: taking off as it swings or within a few ticks of it, with the opponent within jumpWithin. A jump lasts about as long as the weapon takes to come back, so one made then has the fighter coming down just as the next swing is ready. Paid once per swing.

    • chaseCrit

      public float chaseCrit
      A critical hit that comes of a jump made at an opponent it is running after and not getting nearer to: on top of what a critical hit earns. The opponent is chaseFrom to chaseTo blocks off, the fighter has been at a sprint towards it for a quarter of a second and has closed next to nothing, and it has not just hit it (an opponent flying off from a hit is not one that is running). Such a jump is also never charged as wasted (wastedJump), whatever comes of it.

      Why: a run does not catch a player who is backing off or running, and a running jump does; the hit made coming down from it is a critical hit, which does not send that player on its way as a sprint hit would. But a jump that is tried and comes to nothing costs, everywhere, and so the first thing ever learned about jumping was not to (four runs of 0.14.0, each time within fifty updates). Here, and only here, trying is free. Being hit in the air is not: an opponent that backs off with its sword ready still makes a careless jump cost what a hit costs. Zero: no such thing.

      public float spaceIn
      Spacing: paid once per swing of the opponent's, on the step it walks into reach while that sword is on its way back (StepFacts.walkedInOnCooldown): out of reach while the other sword is ready, in while it comes back. While above zero, reengage is paid only into such a sword; coming back in on a ready one is left to what comes of it. The user, 18 October: "Let it learn to space other". Zero (off) unless set.

    • spaceOut

      public float spaceOut
      Spacing, the other half: taken on each step it walks into reach while the opponent's sword is ready (StepFacts.walkedInOnReady). The user, 19 October: opponents space it, crit it and sprint-hit it, because it walks into a ready sword; a day of spaceIn alone left it doing that twice as often as walking in on one coming back. Zero (off) unless set.

    • jumpInReady

      public float jumpInReady
      Paid when the opponent jumps in at it while its sword is ready to meet the jump (a hit then knocks the opponent out of the air and its critical hit never lands), taken when the sword is down. The spacer comes in on its own clock whatever the fighter's sword is doing; trading at its landing leaves the sword down for its next jump in (20 October). Zero (off) unless set.

    • primed

      public float primed
      Per tick with the weapon nearly recharged, the opponent within primedWithin and the sprint in place as the server knows it, so that the hit about to be made will knock back. This is what makes it press W and sprint again before a hit even when the opponent is already in its face and no step forward seems needed. Paid for a few ticks per landed hit only, so standing ready without ever hitting earns nothing.

    • primedWithin

      public float primedWithin

    • closeWithin

      public float closeWithin
      Hits made from nearer than this count as close ones in the metrics.

    • mixStrafe

      public float mixStrafe
      Per tick with the opponent in view and no farther off than mixWithin: paid for strafing the way the plan says, charged for the other way.

    • mixWithin

      public float mixWithin
      Strafing is footwork for a fight; beyond this distance the plan pays nothing and costs nothing. Out of reach it runs straight in (see StraightIn), so that is where the plan ends. Was 5 up to 18 October.

    • mixTiming

      public float mixTiming
      Charged for every swing made while the plan still says to hold it back.
